title: SearXNG local stack - lifecycle contract
description: Bring a self-hosted SearXNG up on this machine without Docker, report on it, or stop it. This is process control, not a search path: it clones upstream SearXNG into a state directory, builds a virtualenv, starts the server detached from the caller, and records the resulting URL where the search layer reads it. The server it starts is the thing WEBSEARCH_SEARXNG_URL points at, which is how a SearXNG joins the Layer-1 engine fanout. Emits the same Envelope (meta.layer "searxng") as every other port.

action.description: up: install if this is the first time, start it, and record its URL for the search layer. status: where the state lives and whether the instance answers. down: stop it. 'up' against an instance that already answers only re-records the URL; it never installs over a live server.

reinstall.description: Delete the state directory and rebuild the checkout and virtualenv from scratch. Only meaningful with 'up'.

ref.description: Git branch or tag of upstream SearXNG to clone. null takes its default branch, which is what keeps the engine scrapers current.

SearxngPayload.description: The state of the local stack after the action ran.

action.description: The action that produced this state.

home.description: The state directory holding the checkout, the virtualenv, the settings file, the log, and the pidfile. WEBSEARCH_SEARXNG_HOME sets it; the default is a 'searxng' directory beside WEBSEARCH_ENV_FILE, else the XDG cache.

url.description: Where the instance listens. Always loopback: a local SearXNG is for this machine, and binding it wider would publish an open search proxy.

installed.description: Whether the checkout and virtualenv are present and usable.

pid.description: The running server's process id, or null when nothing is running. It is a session leader, not a child of the caller, which is what lets it outlive the command that started it.

wired.description: The settings file WEBSEARCH_SEARXNG_URL was written into, or null when nothing was written and the caller must export the variable itself. The target is WEBSEARCH_ENV_FILE when configured, else the user config file ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/websearch/.env); the working directory's .env is never written, since it belongs to whatever project you are standing in.

version.description: The running SearXNG version, when it could be read.

engines_active.description: How many engines the instance has enabled.

engines_available.description: How many engines it knows about in total.

log.description: The server's log file, which is where a failed start explains itself.

onions.description: Whether this instance was configured with its onion engines (ahmia, torch) pointed at the Tor SOCKS port. It follows the tor layer: the generated settings file is rewritten and the instance restarted when the switch changes, because SearXNG reads settings only at startup.
